# [Baseline] - WIN - D - Wireless Shared Devices

On shared devices, allows only the networks deployed via Intune. Wi-Fi networks added by users are removed and no new ones can be added.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | Windows |
| Scope | Device (D) — assign to device groups |
| Type | Settings Catalog |
| Assignment | — |
| Source | ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.20 and A.8.1, NIS2 art. 21(2)(e) — Policy CSP Wifi/AllowManualWiFiConfiguration |
| File | [`Baseline_WIN_D_Wireless_Shared_Devices.json`](Baseline_WIN_D_Wireless_Shared_Devices.json) |

> ONLY for shared devices. By default, Windows turns a network that a user adds themselves into an all-user profile: every other user of that device sees that SSID in the list and can connect to it. Reading the password only works as a local administrator, and in this baseline that is limited to the LAPS account (wlapsadmin by default) — but the SSID list itself already reveals where a colleague has been. Per-user profiles do exist in Windows (netsh wlan add profile user=current), but the interface never creates them that way and there is no MDM or Settings Catalog setting that enforces it: the corresponding GPO sits in Wireless Network (IEEE 802.11) Policies and is domain-bound. What is possible is the other way round: only allow networks from Intune. TWO PREREQUISITES. First deploy a Wi-Fi profile via Intune, otherwise the device is offline once this is applied. And never put this policy on laptops: home and hotel networks will then no longer work, and teleworking should simply be possible. Microsoft also warns that existing user-created profiles are removed when it is applied — that is the intent here, but announce it in advance.
